desc:
Shopify app feature development adds new capabilities to an app that already exists without breaking what merchants rely on. Ecom Swift LLC reads your code, agrees the change in writing and delivers it as a pull request in your repository.

## What is Shopify app feature development?

Shopify app feature development is the work of extending a live app: a new admin screen, a new automation, a bulk tool, a webhook-driven update or a setting merchants have asked for. It differs from a first build because the app already has users, data and habits. The new code must fit existing patterns, survive reinstalls and leave current merchants undisturbed.

## Why adding features is riskier than it looks

A live app carries history. Older merchants may have data in a shape you no longer use. Some installs predate a scope change. Webhook handlers may depend on behavior nobody documented. A feature that works in a clean test store can still fail for an older merchant.

That is why careful feature work includes the unglamorous parts: reading the surrounding code, checking migrations, and testing install, reinstall and uninstall paths. A feature is only finished when the old features still work beside it.

## How new features affect your app

Features that answer repeated merchant requests reduce support load and give people a reason to stay on a paid plan. A bulk edit tool saves a merchant hours. A background sync means they stop watching a progress bar. A well-placed setting removes a support email.

Merchants notice reliability more than novelty. One feature that works every time earns more trust than three that work most of the time, so we favor a small, tested change over a large, rushed one.

## What good feature work includes

- A written description of the change before any code, so everyone agrees on the outcome.
- Polaris components and your existing code patterns, so the new screen looks native.
- Admin GraphQL queries and mutations written against a supported API version.
- Webhook handlers for the topics the feature depends on, with verification and retries.
- Background jobs for heavy tasks, so the admin page stays responsive.
- Install and reinstall checks on a development store.
- Automated tests for the new code, in the larger packages.
- A pull request with clear notes, so your team can review each change.
- Release notes written for merchants, if you want them.

## How we work

You tell us what merchants keep asking for. We read the relevant parts of the code, write a short plan and send it for approval. We then build in a branch in your repository, test against a development store and open a pull request. You review, comment and we adjust until it is right.

The Basic package covers one small feature or a few fixes. Standard covers a new admin flow with API calls and webhook support. Premium covers a larger set with background jobs, tests and merchant release notes. If the change touches access scopes, we flag it early, because merchants may need to approve the new permissions.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Collect real merchant requests and rank them by how often they come up.
- Describe the expected result, not only the screen.
- Share any known quirks in the codebase.
- Review the pull request promptly so the work keeps moving.

**Avoid:**
- Bundling unrelated changes into one request.
- Asking for new access scopes unless the feature needs them.
- Skipping the test store step to save time.
- Editing the same files in parallel while we work.

## Who this service is for

Product owners with a backlog and no spare developer. Agencies that run a client app and need a specialist for one release. Founders whose original developer has moved on.

## What we need from you

Repository access, collaborator access to your Partner account if the work touches app settings, a development store and a short written request. We can work in an app another developer built. We never ask for passwords, and access is limited to what the change requires.
